passages.context: Read for the Twelfth Sunday after Pentecost Gradual (Ps 33:2-3 Vulg). On the title Theodoret retells the Nob episode, identifies Abimelech with Abiathar as a man of two names, and reports but rejects the setting before Achis at Geth as not fitting the psalm's words. On v. 2: fleeing or pursuing, in good fortune or ill, I hymn my Master; on v. 3 with v. 4 he makes the sharers of his meekness sharers of his singing.

passages.context: The complete exposition was read for the Twelfth Sunday after Pentecost Introit (Ps 69:2-4 Vulg). Theodoret sets the psalm historically - David fleeing Absalom, stung more by the memory of his sin than by his enemies - and notes that the title's in rememorationem stands in some copies but not in the Hebrew or the other translators. On v. 2 the speaker asks swift help because many and various calamities engulf him; on v. 3 the enemies are to be cheated of their hope. Migne's apparatus at v. 2 records that the Domine ad adjuvandum clause is absent from LXX codd. Vat. and Alex. but stands in the Hebrew, Apollinaris and Augustine, and a manuscript addition printed in the notes applies the psalm to the martyrs.

passages.context: Read for the Twelfth Sunday after Pentecost Alleluia (Ps 87:2 Vulg). Theodoret's hypothesis: the prophecy foretells the Jews' calamities and the Babylonian servitude and at the same time teaches the pains of all human nature after sin - no Passion reading. The title is handled philologically (Symmachus per chorum; Aiman a choirmaster, citing 1 Par 6). On the appointed verse: knowing the Lord as the God of my salvation, I beg night and day that my supplication be received.

passages.context: Read for the Twelfth Sunday after Pentecost Communion (Ps 103:13-15 Vulg). Theodoret reads the psalm as a hymn of the one Creator's common benefits. On the appointed verses his reading is purely providential: God supplies rain so that the earth brings forth every kind of fruit - bread to strengthen and nourish human nature, wine to gladden and make life sweeter, oil to nourish within and brighten without - quoting Symmachus's clearer rendering. No sacramental turn on these verses.
